added_models.model: Human whole-blood ex vivo assays (anti-IgE basophil degranulation, B-cell CD69) for seletalisib

engagement.judgement: Opening year set to the first human study that used the assay ex vivo, since the in-vitro data were unpublished until 2017.
engagement.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: first-in-human Study-1 ethics reference 13/SC/0366 (2013); the assay paper was published April 2017. Abstract read.
engagement.quote: In human whole blood assays, seletalisib inhibited CD69 expression upon B-cell activation and anti-IgE-mediated basophil degranulation.
engagement.note: UCB's human whole-blood assays showed seletalisib blocking anti-IgE basophil degranulation and B-cell CD69 before first-in-human dosing.

engagement.magnitude_basis: ex vivo anti-IgE basophil CD63 inhibition in dosed subjects vs in-vitro whole-blood inhibition (no shared potency figure)
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Helmer reuses the whole-blood basophil assay ex vivo but does not set it beside the in-vitro potency, so comparison_stated false. Ex-vivo blockade of a stimulus, so readout_tier direct.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5384962). Authors note high inter-subject variability limiting the assay's value for dose selection; subjects were healthy volunteers and mild psoriasis, not Sjögren's.
engagement.quote: The ex vivo stimulation of basophil degranulation inhibition demonstrated in Study-1 suggested that PI3Kδ inhibition was achieved at all tested doses of seletalisib.
engagement.note: Healthy adults and psoriasis patients dosed with seletalisib showed ex vivo inhibition of basophil degranulation, the whole-blood assay's readout.
engagement.reason: Ex vivo degranulation fell in dosed humans

added_models.model: Whole-blood B-cell activation assays (pAkt, CD69; human in vitro, rat and monkey ex vivo) for leniolisib

engagement.judgement: Rat and monkey ex vivo whole-blood readouts kept on the same track as the human in-vitro assay: one readout (B-cell pAkt/CD69 in whole blood).
engagement.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: NCT02775916 (Sjögren's) started June 2016; the assay was in use for first-in-human Study 2101 earlier, date not found. Abstract read; FDA review (2023) describes the human, rat and monkey whole-blood pAkt/CD69 assays.
engagement.quote: In vivo, CDZ173 inhibits B cell activation in rats and monkeys in a concentration- and time-dependent manner.
engagement.note: Novartis whole-blood B-cell activation assays (pAkt, CD69) in human blood in vitro and rats and monkeys dosed in vivo preceded the Sjögren's Phase 2.

engagement.magnitude_basis: ex vivo pAkt/pS6 reduction in dosed patients vs in-vitro whole-blood inhibition (no shared potency figure)
engagement.judgement: Engagement accepts any dosed humans, so APDS patients count; the Sjögren's Study 2203 pAkt data are unpublished and not scored. Paired by me, comparison_stated false.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (epub 2017-09-29). Patients had APDS, not Sjögren's. FDA review NDA 217759 (2023) reports ~90% maximal ex vivo pAkt inhibition at 70-140 mg BID in healthy volunteers (Study 2101) and says pAkt was measured in Sjögren's Study 2203, but gives no Sjögren's result.
engagement.quote: Oral leniolisib led to a dose-dependent reduction in PI3K/AKT pathway activity assessed ex vivo and improved immune dysregulation.
engagement.note: Leniolisib-dosed APDS patients showed dose-dependent ex vivo reduction of PI3K/AKT activity, as the whole-blood assays predicted; FDA later confirmed it in healthy volunteers.
engagement.short: Dosed humans: ex vivo pAkt fell
engagement.reason: Ex vivo pAkt fell in dosed humans
